articles.title: Ram Mandir Probe: SIT Intensifies Ayodhya Land Deal Investigation Ahead of July 15 Report Deadline
articles.description: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has returned to Ayodhya to intensify its investigation into alleged irregularities linked to land purchases made by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. The fresh round of inquiries comes as the SIT prepares to submit its final report by July 15, focusing on land acquisition documents, payment records, and witness statements. According to sources, the SIT questioned Trust member Gopal Rao regarding documents related to land transactions. Trustee Dr. Anil Mishra was also questioned for nearly eight hours as investigators examined records connected to land purchases and payment procedures. Officials are scrutinizing whether certain parcels of land were acquired at prices significantly higher than their reported market value. The investigation is expected to expand further, with the SIT likely to question Champat Rai, the Trust's General Secretary, to seek his response to allegations surrounding the purchase of land. Investigators are examining the rationale behind the transactions and verifying whether all procedures complied with legal and administrative norms.\ Sources indicate that the SIT is also identifying and interviewing witnesses connected to the land deals while reviewing documentary evidence collected during previous visits. The renewed inquiry follows an earlier phase of investigation, during which officials gathered preliminary records before moving to detailed verification. Alongside the land transaction probe, a separate investigation into the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Temple is also progressing. Police continue questioning accused Avinash Shukla while he remains in custody, seeking additional evidence related to the alleged misappropriation of donations. With two parallel investigations underway—one concerning land purchases and another involving alleged theft of temple offerings—authorities are working to complete evidence collection before submitting their findings. Officials have not announced any conclusions, and the investigations remain ongoing as investigators continue examining documents, witnesses, and financial records.
